heldClaims.claimText: Historical rule (Academic Integrity Policy 2022 as described in the Teaching@Sydney FAQ): students could only use assistance, including automated writing tools, if the unit of study outline expressly permitted it. Current student guidance (updated 2 June 2026) instead allows AI in open assessments and generally prohibits it in secure assessments unless expressly permitted, so this undated prior-permission rule is held as historical and not shown as a current university-wide rule. The current Policy Register text was not re-read clause by clause.

topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: Each unit outline has a 'Use of AI' column for every assessment. AI can be used in open (unsupervised) assessments, where educators guide appropriate use and use must be acknowledged; it generally cannot be used in secure (supervised) assessments unless the unit coordinator expressly permits it. These coursework rules do not apply to HDR theses.
topics.scope: Open/secure assessment lanes and the unit outline 'Use of AI' column.

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.summary: AI used in assessments must be acknowledged, including AI translation, paraphrasing or referencing tools; basic spelling/grammar correction and word processing are exempt. The statement gives the tool name and version, publisher, URL and how it was used; coordinators may require logs. HDR theses must include an AI statement even if no AI was used.
topics.scope: Acknowledgement content and HDR thesis statement.

claims.text: If University of Sydney students use AI in assessments they must acknowledge it, including generative AI translation, paraphrasing or referencing tools; tools used only for word processing or basic spelling and grammar correction need not be acknowledged. Where permitted by the unit outline, the statement must say that AI tools were used and give the tool's name and version, the publisher, the URL and a brief description of how it was used; unit coordinators may add requirements such as a log of AI inputs and outputs.

evidence.quote: If you use AI in your assessments, you're required to acknowledge it – this includes acknowledging any tools that use generative AI, such as translation tools, paraphrasing tools or referencing tools. You are not required to acknowledge tools used for word processing, or which only correct basic spelling and grammar.

additionalTopics.title: Academic integrity & procedures
additionalTopics.summary: Inappropriately generating content with AI is an academic integrity breach and AI-generated submissions may be treated as contract cheating. Turnitin's AI detector may be used, but its score is never the only evidence. Minor breaches may be handled by the unit coordinator, more serious ones by the faculty Educational Integrity team, and the most serious by the Registrar. Academic decisions: faculty/Academic Panel review within 20 working days, then SAB within 15 working days; Registrar misconduct penalties: SDAC appeal within 20 working days.
additionalTopics.scope: Integrity breaches, investigation levels and appeal routes.

claims.text: The University of Sydney's Academic Integrity Policy 2022 states it is an academic integrity breach to inappropriately generate content using artificial intelligence to complete an assessment task, and submitting an assessment generated by AI may be considered contract cheating.

evidence.quote: Clause 4(9)(2)(j)(i) states that it is an academic integrity breach to inappropriately generate content using artificial intelligence to complete an assessment task. Clause 4(13)(1)(i) states that submitting an assessment generated by AI may be considered contract cheating.
evidence.title: Frequently asked questions about generative AI at Sydney
evidence.location: The policy and assessment frameworks section, 'What is in the policy about generative AI use by students?'

claims.text: The University of Sydney advises that Turnitin's AI detection tool may be used if a marker suspects AI-generated work where its use was not permitted or not acknowledged, but the AI detector score would not be the only evidence relied upon for an academic integrity case.

evidence.quote: If a marker or teacher suspects that part or all of your assessment has been generated using AI technology and its use was not permitted, or use was not acknowledged, the Turnitin AI detection tool may be used to evaluate the situation. It's important to note that the AI detector score would not be the only evidence relied upon for an academic integrity case, but will be considered alongside other relevant evidence.
evidence.title: Using artificial intelligence tools responsibly
evidence.location: Detecting generative AI use section

claims.text: At the University of Sydney, minor academic integrity breaches may be handled locally by unit coordinators, more serious ones are investigated by the faculty Educational Integrity team, and the most serious suspected cheating is handled by the Registrar under the Student Discipline Rule. Students may bring a support person to an integrity meeting.

evidence.quote: Some minor breaches can be handled by unit coordinators locally while more serious breaches are referred to the relevant faculty’s Educational Integrity Coordinator or one of its nominated academics for investigation.
evidence.title: Detection and investigation of academic integrity breaches (last updated 2 June 2026)

evidence.quote: The most serious instances of suspected cheating are handled under the misconduct process, which is governed by the University of Sydney (Student Discipline) Rule and handled by the Registrar.
evidence.title: Detection and investigation of academic integrity breaches (last updated 2 June 2026)
evidence.location: Who investigates; lines 34-34 of captured page text

claims.text: University of Sydney academic decisions and misconduct findings use different review routes. For academic decisions, students may apply for faculty or Academic Panel review within 20 working days, and may appeal to the Student Appeals Body (SAB) within 15 working days of the review outcome, but not simply because they disagree with it. Where the Registrar makes a misconduct finding or penalty, the student may appeal to the Student Disciplinary Appeals Committee (SDAC) within 20 working days of the penalty notice. Not every AI-related academic integrity matter is a Registrar misconduct decision.

evidence.quote:
